title: Regional Earthquake Forecasting
subtitle: Can machine learning beat a statistical baseline?
summary: A statistics and machine-learning study on 17,229 USGS earthquakes (2020–2025) asking whether ML improves monthly earthquake-occurrence probabilities across 60 regional grid cells, compared against Poisson baselines.
result: Logistic regression reached a 0.0867 Brier score on held-out 2025 data versus 0.0915 for the Poisson baseline (5.3% lower error), though the bootstrap interval includes zero, so the improvement isn't conclusive.
highlights: Leakage-safe time split: train 2021–23, validate 2024, test Jan–Nov 2025
Compared Poisson baselines, logistic regression and gradient boosting on Brier score, log loss, calibration and AUC
Reproducible Python pipeline, written report and an interactive static dashboard (original C++ prototype included)

visual.alt: Line chart of observed versus predicted fraction of active regions per month in 2025; the logistic-regression forecast stays near 0.22 while observed values range from 0.20 to 0.28.

title: Huawei Two-Week Challenge
subtitle: Scheduling LLM inference across an edge server and remote servers
summary: An interactive, event-driven scheduler written in C++ for Huawei's two-week programming challenge. Every frame it reads arrival, transfer and completion events from the judge, then decides what runs next on a local edge server and on K remote servers, as each request moves through prefill and decode phases with network transfers in between.
highlights: Tracks every request through an 18-state lifecycle: pre-processing, layer-by-layer processing and post-processing for both prefill and decode, plus uploads and downloads
Baseline policy: oldest-ready-first on every server, with new requests placed on the least-loaded remote server
Speaks the judge's interactive frame-by-frame protocol, reading events and emitting task assignments
